Subject: HelixHealth IP claim notice: evidence set + timeline request

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a separate item that landed with our legal team: a third‑party notice alleging that a small portion of the models we use together could implicate a prior patent claim. We're not making a legal conclusion yet, but our counsel asked us to collect evidence and confirm contract responsibilities under the Order Form / MSA (defend, indemnify, evidence cooperation).

Please see the attached: a zip with the claim notice from the third party and our internal triage notes (Helix_Helpdesk_Evidence.zip). Our counsel needs: a) confirmation of Redwood's proposed defense/control posture if the claim proceeds, b) an estimated timeline for assembling your technical evidence (model provenance, training provenance logs, inference logs for the implicated tenant), and c) any redline language you will insist on in the upcoming Order Form v3 to allocate risk.

We are on a compressed timeline: procurement would like the parties to agree to a mutual action plan and Order Form redlines by end of next week (target: 2028-02-23). Can Redwood commit to a point person and a first pass redline by 2028-02-17?

Thanks —
Maya Trivedi
Sr. Counsel, HelixHealth
maya.trivedi@helixhealth.com

Subject: RE: HelixHealth IP claim notice: evidence set + timeline request

Maya / team —

Thanks, Maya. We reviewed the zip. From a contract perspective, the MSA (Sec. 7) and the pending Order Form v3 are the right places to clarify responsibility for third‑party IP claims and evidence cooperation. High level thoughts:

1) Defense vs. control: Redwood is generally willing to provide a defense for covered third‑party infringement claims but will seek 'reasonable' control of the defense when the claim implicates model provenance — we will propose a split approach in the redline: a) Redwood defends/controls where the claim arises from our hosted model variant and codebase; b) customer defense for claims arising from customer‑supplied prompt engineering or customer models.

2) Evidence handback / timelines: we can produce inference logs & model manifests within 10 business days for standard tenants; for historical training provenance we may need escalation and an extended window (30 business days) depending on retention. We'll propose a graduated timeline in the MAP.

3) Cap & insurance: expect Redwood to propose a limited indemnity (cap tied to fees) and to request notice + cooperation language. We'll push back on open‑ended indemnities.

I'll attach a first pass redline and a mutual action plan (MAP) workbook. Jonas — can you confirm the tenant id and whether Helix has any special log-retention settings that would affect the 10‑day pull?

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf, Helix-Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx

From: Maya Trivedi <maya.trivedi@helixhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: HelixHealth IP claim notice: evidence set + timeline request

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear note and the draft redline. A few quick points from Helix counsel and procurement:
- Defense control: Helix prefers Redwood to take full control only if Redwood's hosted model is the proximate cause; otherwise Helix needs the right to select counsel. We'll review your split approach but will likely ask for stronger customer‑control protections.
- Timeline: 10 business days for inference logs is acceptable. Training provenance in 30 business days is a stretch but workable if Redwood provides a weekly status update.
- Cap: procurement wants an explicit dollar cap equal to 12 months of fees or an insurance‑backed alternative; they are resistant to a fee‑tied cap without minimums.

We do accept your proposed redline as a starting point. Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide the redline as a tracked PDF and a DocuSign-ready order form by 2028‑02‑21 so our internal approvers can validate changes in one pass.

Maya
Maya Trivedi
Sr. Counsel, HelixHealth
Attachment: (none)

2) Kimberly attached the redline and MAP files yesterday (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf; Helix-Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx). Per Maya's ask, legal will publish a tracked PDF and an editable order form for DocuSign by EOD 2028‑02‑21.

3) Outstanding commercial pivot items for exec awareness: a) Helix pushing for a 12‑month fee cap or insurance alternative; b) defense‑control nuance — they want stronger customer selection rights if the claim is not clearly Redwood‑hosted. Recommend we offer the 12‑month fee cap as an alternative if Helix will accept a narrower scope of indemnity for AI‑generated output; also offer a joint counsel-selection clause with Redwood having initial control for Redwood‑hosted claims.

I'll send a short internal note to GTM and Legal summarizing the approach after this thread. Jonas — please post the redacted evidence link and confirm whether any logs need an NDA/technical appendix to be shared.
